# Advertise audit-lease capability and refuse old peers

Implements WL-0MWJ7QYX0001KAQX **AC4** (producer answer Q3-A: advertise
lease-support through the coordination check-in; the leader refuses audit
dispatch to peers lacking it — fail-closed).

## Context

Work-item panes run `npx tsx src/start.ts` and hold their module graph for
days. A host whose pane predates the lease change
(WL-0MWFJH3NW006F5GN) runs availability-only admission — the exact
cross-host race the lease gate removes — with no version signal. The
coordination check-in (`coordination.ts` v2 entries +
`downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts`) carries `offers` but no
capability/version field, so the leader cannot tell an old peer from a new
one before dispatching its audit offers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Workers advertise audit-lease support through the coordination check-in as an additive capability field on `CoordinationEntry` (absent for legacy entries, so old readers/writers interoperate).
- The leader refuses audit dispatch to peers that do not advertise lease support (fail-closed): an old host (predating WL-0MWFJH3NW006F5GN) cannot be the dispatch path for an audit, so the availability-only race it would run is closed.
- A peer without the capability is refused for audits but its non-audit offers (implement/prep) still flow unchanged.
- Legacy entries without the field remain readable and an old peer is refused, never crashes the leader — pinned by an interop test (legacy entry shape + no-capability peer).
- The refusal surfaces on the coordination decision/attribution path with a distinct gate token (e.g. `lease-capability-absent`), so the leader's refusal is observable.
- This fail-closed gate is the only intended behaviour change for old hosts; the full herdr test suite stays green with this change.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts` — `CoordinationEntry` (`:111`) gains the additive capability field.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-checkin.ts` — the check-in writes the field.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — the offer-admission loop (`:538`-ish, `rejectOffer` `:311`) refuses audit offers of peers lacking the capability.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts` — offer computation (`computeMostImportantItem`).
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination.test.ts`, `coordination-leader.test.ts`, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `machine-coordination.test.ts` — interop + refusal pinning.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — coordination capability paragraph.

## Impact

A stale host can no longer silently reintroduce the double-audit race: the fleet refuses audits through old peers instead of hoping they upgraded.
data.title: Advertise audit-lease capability and refuse old peers

# Saturated pre-check refusal carries the derived cooldown

Implements WL-0MWJ7QYX0001KAQX **AC3** (producer answer Q2-A: derive on the
pre-check refusal from the availability payload's held lease, keeping
"refused availability never churns a lease").

## Context

The 429 `retry_after_s` is carried on the admission refusal
(`host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts:462`) and the orchestrator decision entry
(`downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts:734`) — but the pre-check refuses
BEFORE admission whenever availability reports `available:false`, which is
exactly the state a held foreign lease produces. So the admission `saturated`
arm and its `retryAfterS` deferral rarely run, and the pre-check refusal names
no cooldown at all.

The availability contract already pins `leases[].expiresAt` as epoch
milliseconds (`downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts:73-87`), read
through a tolerant normaliser — the derivation source exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the availability read reports `available:false` (the state a held foreign lease produces), the pre-check refusal derives `retryAfterS` from the held lease's `leases[].expiresAt` (epoch ms → seconds) and surfaces it on the decision entry exactly like the admission 429 arm does.
- No extra proxy calls: the acquire is still only attempted when the pre-check admits.
- Pinned with a captured payload test (held-lease availability → refusal with the derived cooldown), plus a test that the existing admission-carried `retryAfterS` surface is unchanged.
- A malformed or already-past `expiresAt` clamps to a sane cooldown (>= 0) and never throws on the pre-check path.
- If the live proxy serves `leases: []` while saturated, the derivation degrades to "no cooldown named" and this is reported on the child rather than silently dropped.
- No other dispatch behaviour change, and the full herdr test suite stays green with this change.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getActiveAudit` (`:789`) and the returned `DowntimeActiveAuditResult`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts` — `DowntimeActiveAuditResult` (`:782`) gains the cooldown evidence.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.ts` — `:710` pre-check consumption, refusal/decision shape.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator-dispatch.ts` — the decision entry that carries `retryAfterS` (`:731`).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts` — `AuditAvailabilityLease.expiresAt` (epoch ms).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.test.ts`, `audit-availability.cross-host.test.ts` — captured-payload pinning.

## Impact

A saturated audit refusal now names its cooldown on the common path, so an operator can tell when the tier re-checks without reading the code.
data.title: Saturated pre-check refusal carries the derived cooldown

# Dispatcher unevenly distributes downtime work across projects

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher is documented to share idle capacity across registered
projects by **global cross-project round-robin** ("no single project can
monopolise the downtime worker"), but measured dispatch history shows the
opposite: on each of the last three nights one project consumed roughly half of
all dispatches in long consecutive runs, while other registered projects with
live coordination entries were dispatched rarely or not at all.

Measured from every project's `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` on this
machine (rows with a `paneId`, i.e. dispatches that actually produced a pane):

| Night | Total | Distribution | Longest consecutive run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-11-15 | 47 | AI_Hell 24, ContextHub 22, games_curator 1 | AI_Hell 11, ContextHub 9 |
| 2026-11-16 | 91 | games_curator 35, tce-the-rising 23, ContextHub 19, AI_Hell 14 | games_curator 5, tce-the-rising 5, 4 |
| 2026-11-17 | 96 | **SorraAgents 48**, tce-the-rising 16, games_curator 14, AI_Hell 10, ContextHub 8 | **SorraAgents 9, 8, 8, 6, 4, 3** |

Two further facts sharpen the picture:

- Every SorraAgents dispatch on 2026-11-17 was a **prep-tier** kind (21
  `intake`, 22 `plan`, 5 `risk-effort`) and none was `implement` or `audit`,
  whereas every other project's dispatches that day were dominated by
  `implement`/`audit`.
- The round-robin cursor (`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`)
  **is** being written — so this is not a repeat of the "cursor never wired"
  defect (WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK) nor of the "charge at selection, not at
  dispatch" defect (WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN). The residual behaviour is still
  unfair after both fixes landed.

## Users

- **As the producer**, I want idle machine capacity to rotate across every
  project that has dispatchable work, so that a project with a large backlog of
  one stage cannot consume the whole night while other projects' ready work
  waits, and so that standup reports are not dominated by a single project.
- **As a project owner (agent or human) watching a project go undispatched for
  a day**, I want to see *why* my project was skipped — a hold, a deep review
  queue, or a fairness defect — from the dispatch and decision logs, rather
  than guessing.
- **As the dispatcher maintainer**, I want the fairness rule to be enforced by
  the code path that actually chooses what to dispatch, with a test that fails
  when one project wins several consecutive slots while a peer has an
  admissible offer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The dispatch selection path is documented and tested such that, when two or more projects have admissible offers and surplus capacity exists, no project is dispatched more than twice in succession; a failing-first test drives a coordination file with four roots holding interleaved admissible/held offers and asserts the bound.
- The residual bias is identified with evidence and one of the two candidate mechanisms below is either confirmed and fixed, or ruled out with recorded evidence: (a) rotation applies only to the tick's selected root, so when that root's offers are all held the leader falls through the remaining entries in raw coordination-file order; (b) prep-tier offers (`intake`/`plan`/`risk-effort`) are never held by the review-queue, CPU or audit-slot gates while `implement`/`audit` offers are, so a project with a large prep backlog wins every slot on a machine whose other projects have mature implement/audit backlogs.
- A per-project fairness metric is recorded on every dispatch decision (selected root, dispatching root, tick outcome, and the consecutive-run length for the dispatching root) so the distribution can be audited after the fact from `downtime-dispatches.log` or the coordination decision log without replaying logs by hand.
- Fairness accounting does not regress the existing overrides: critical-first dispatch, priority ordering, the review-queue depth gate, the audit slot minimum, the code-freeze split-by-skill, and the host-wide dispatch budget all behave exactly as they do today; each has a test asserting it still wins over round-robin rotation.
- The observed concentration is re-measured after the fix and reported on the work item: over a comparable window with at least three active projects, no project exceeds twice its even share of dispatches, and no project holds a consecutive run longer than the bound in AC1.
- New and updated tests cover the fairness invariant, the two candidate mechanisms, the overrides in AC4, and the fairness metric in AC3.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The producer can trust that a night of idle machine time is shared across every project that has ready work, instead of one project absorbing half the night's dispatches while the others wait.

## Constraints

- **No new scheduler.** Fix the existing leader selection path (`selectLeastRecentlyServed` + the entry loop in `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts`); do not introduce per-tier cursors, a second ranking, or a new queue.
- **Preserve every existing gate.** Producer-review, attempt-budget, non-terminal cooldown, code-freeze, CPU saturation, audit slot minimum, in-flight and review-queue holds are sequential filters with established semantics (WL-0MWDDHVN and successors) and must not be relaxed, reordered or duplicated to buy fairness.
- **Fail-open fairness.** A cursor read/write failure, a lock timeout or a corrupt cursor file must never block or fail a dispatch; the tick degrades to today's behaviour.
- **On-disk cursor format unchanged.** `{ "<worklogRoot>": "<ISO-8601>" }` in `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`; no migration, so live machine state stays valid.
- **Hot path budget.** No additional `wl` spawns per tick; at most one extra coordination-lock acquisition per consumed offer.
- **Scope guard.** Any additional unfairness found outside the leader selection path (for example the own-backlog fallback tracked by WL-0MWAJ3RPX000HQIG) is recorded as a separate work item, not folded in.

## Existing state

- `selectLeastRecentlyServed` (`downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts`) is a pure read: unknown roots sort first, otherwise the oldest timestamp wins, ties broken alphabetically.
- The leader rotates **only the selected root** to the front of the entry list and then iterates the rest in coordination-file order; it returns after the first successful dispatch, so a tick dispatches at most one item.
- The cursor is charged only on a consumed offer (`isConsumedDispatchOutcome`), never at selection — deliberate, per WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN.
- A root that is selected but whose offers are all held is never charged, so it stays first in the rotation indefinitely, and the fall-through order behind it is not round-robin.
- The decision log records per-offer rejections with gate tokens, but not the selected root, the dispatching root, or any run-length accounting; log rotation (500 lines per project) discards the evidence within hours, so past nights cannot be re-audited from the logs.
- Two adjacent defects are already fixed and must not be re-litigated: the cursor was never wired into the dispatch path (WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK) and the post-dispatch charge was dead code (WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN).

## Desired change

A leader selection path in which the rotation is applied to the **whole** ordered candidate set rather than only to the tick's first choice, so that a root whose offers are held cannot silently degrade selection to coordination-file order; plus enough recorded fairness evidence (selected root, dispatching root, run length) to audit any night after the fact.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` — Selection is a pure read over the cursor; needs to expose an ordered candidate list (not just the single least-recently-served root) if the fix rotates the whole set.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts` — The entry rotation, per-offer filter chain and dispatch loop (~490–810); this is where fall-through order is decided and where a run-length bound would be enforced.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.selection.ts` — `advanceRoundRobinCursor` and the shared `isConsumedDispatchOutcome` charge predicate (~619–666).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.offer-selection.ts` — `orderAdmissibleOffers`, the per-entry drain-aware tie-break that decides which of one entry's offers is tried first.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.head-scan.ts` — The registered-root sweep's own round-robin usage (~420–510); must obey the same fairness rule.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.log-coordination.ts` / `downtime-log-coordination.ts` — Coordination decision entry shape; needs the fairness fields from AC3.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — *Fair scheduling: global cross-project round-robin* section (~4050–4130); states the guarantee that measurement shows is not met.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: fairness flapping the other way.** Forcing rotation can dispatch low-value prep work ahead of a mature project's ready `implement` item, and can slow a project that is the only one with work. Mitigation: the rotation only reorders *candidates that are already admissible*, and the existing priority/critical overrides still win (AC4).
- **Risk: cursor state carries no "held" information.** A root can look "least recently served" forever because holds are never charged; a naive fix would ping-pong between two starving roots. Mitigation: the four-root interleaved test in AC1 pins the behaviour.
- **Risk: log rotation destroys the evidence mid-investigation.** Mitigation: capture the 2026-11-15/16/17 per-project dispatch-log aggregates on the work item before changing code (the numbers in this brief are that capture).
- **Risk: the measured imbalance is partly legitimate.** A project genuinely holding all dispatchable work *should* be dispatched. Mitigation: AC5 re-measures with at least three active projects and compares against even share, not against zero.
- **Assumption (documented, not confirmed by a producer):** "fair" means an **even share of dispatch slots among projects that have admissible offers**, with critical-first and priority overrides preserved — this is the reading already stated in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, so the brief does not block on it. See the OPEN QUESTION in the Appendix.
- **Assumption:** the per-project dispatch logs on this machine are a complete record of dispatches (they are written by the dispatching instance and agree with the round-robin cursor's accounting identity).
- **Scope-creep guard:** removing the own-backlog fallback (WL-0MWAJ3RPX000HQIG) and increasing per-project slot budgets are separate items; this item changes selection fairness only.

## Related work

Automated report (find-related skill):

### Related work items
- **WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK** – RCA: herdr round-robin dispatch across multiple projects not working (completed)
- **WL-0MNGR0E6E000ZVEQ** – Fix AMPA start-work failure: CONTAINER_PROJECT_ROOT undefined (completed)
- **WL-0MTRBOU0Y002M2CX** – Downtime dispatches land in Podcast workspace instead of Dispatcher workspace (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: algorithm, dispatch, dispatcher, dispatches, distribute (+12 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: dispatch, dispatcher, dispatches, distribute, evaluate (+9 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: algorithm, dispatch, dispatcher, example, identify (+7 more)

Additional related work identified during intake (read directly, not part of the
automated report):

- **WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN** (completed) — *Downtime round-robin: post-dispatch cursor charge is dead code, so one project can monopolise the dispatcher.* Same symptom class, adjacent cause (charge point); its own Risks section predicted this residual: "a root that never dispatches is never charged, so it stays first in the rotation indefinitely". This item covers what remained after that fix.
- **WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK** (completed) — RCA that first found the cursor was never wired into the dispatch path. The wiring exists now, so this item is not a duplicate.
- **WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2** (completed) — retired the per-tier `sortEntriesByRoundRobin` second ranking in favour of offer-removal + re-offer; explains why rotation now lives only in the leader entry loop.
- **WL-0MWAJ3RPX000HQIG** (open, low) — whether to remove the own-backlog fallback; a related but separate fairness surface (only 2 of 96 dispatches on 2026-11-17 came from that path).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — *Fair scheduling: global cross-project round-robin* and *Critical-first dispatch* sections define the guarantee this item measures.
- `docs/dev/release-dispatch-budget-evaluation.md` — the host-wide dispatch budget that must keep precedence over rotation.

Duplicate-work check: performed with `wl search` on `round-robin`, `fairness`,
`dispatcher`, `dispatch imbalance`. No open item covers this gap; the completed
items above are partial overlap only, so the ACs here are scoped to the residual
behaviour rather than rewritten from an existing item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The work item was created by the producer and dispatched automatically by the
herdr downtime worker; no interactive interview round took place in this
session. No question was answered by a human in this session.

- Q: "What does 'fair' mean here — an even share of dispatch slots per project with admissible work, a share weighted by each project's dispatchable backlog depth, or a share weighted by item priority?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (no producer response in this session). Research: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` states the intent as *global cross-project round-robin* with the explicit goal that "no single project can monopolise the downtime worker", and WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V's ACs describe alternating dispatch with a priority override. Working assumption for this brief: even share among projects with admissible offers, priority/critical overrides preserved. If the producer prefers backlog-weighted fairness, AC1/AC5 change but the rest of the brief stands.
- Q: "Is the imbalance the round-robin algorithm being wrong, or a genuine scarcity of admissible work on the other projects?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (self-answered as far as the evidence allows). Research: the two candidate mechanisms in AC2 are both consistent with the measured data; the 2026-11-17 split (all SorraAgents dispatches prep-tier, all other projects' dispatches implement/audit-dominated) points at gate asymmetry at least as much as at ordering. The brief therefore requires confirming or ruling out both mechanisms with evidence rather than assuming one.
- Q: "Should the fix also cover the own-backlog fallback and per-project slot budgets?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: only 2 of 96 dispatches on 2026-11-17 came from `own-backlog-fallback`, and slot budgets are per-project configuration rather than a scheduling rule. Both are out of scope here and already tracked (WL-0MWAJ3RPX000HQIG for the fallback).

### Plan session — 2026-11-17 (agent `plan`, session `herdr-1794934614-3693221-32084`)

This planning run was dispatching-driven (no interactive producer in the
session), so no new interview round took place. The three OPEN QUESTIONs above
were re-reviewed rather than re-asked; each is dispositioned here:

- **Q1 "what does fair mean"** — **NOT BLOCKING.** AC1 pins the concrete
  behaviour (no project dispatched more than twice in succession while a peer
  has an admissible offer and surplus capacity exists) and AC5 pins the
  threshold (no project beyond twice its even share). The working assumption
  (even share among projects with admissible offers, overrides preserved) is
  the documented intent in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and is now
  exercised by the override-precedence regression tests. If the producer wants
  backlog-weighted fairness instead, AC1/AC5 change but the decomposition
  stands.
- **Q2 "algorithm wrong, or genuine scarcity?"** — **RESOLVED BY PLANNING,
  not by assumption.** This is exactly what the diagnosis child
  (WL-0MWKY0R4Z004UU85) must answer with evidence; the plan deliberately does
  not pre-commit to a mechanism.
- **Q3 "also cover own-backlog fallback and slot budgets?"** — **OUT OF
  SCOPE, confirmed.** The parent's scope guard and the existing
  WL-0MWAJ3RPX000HQIG carry the fallback; slot budgets are configuration, not
  a scheduling rule. No child touches them.

**Phasing note.** This item is confined to one package (`packages/herdr`) with
one deployable behaviour, so the phases are test-first slices inside that
component (diagnosis + characterisation → override guards → failing invariant
test → instrumentation → fix → asymmetry resolution → docs → re-measurement)
rather than cross-service vertical slices. Between phases the next child's
description is reviewed and updated before work starts.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-17T17:00Z — Plan session decomposed the item into 8 children
  (5 test/verification or instrumentation items before the fix), wired
  dependencies in test-first order, and verified 100% parent AC coverage
  (8/8 ACs mapped, `tree_coverage` review: `proceed`).

| # | Child | Type | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | WL-0MWKY0R4Z004UU85 — Diagnose residual dispatch-unfairness mechanism | task | — |
| 2 | WL-0MWKY0VF5003ZKRO — Override-precedence regression tests for dispatch fairness | task | — |
| 3 | WL-0MWKY0ZQI004UZXR — Failing-first fairness invariant test (four roots) | task | — |
| 4 | WL-0MWKY141H002LULI — Record per-project fairness metric on dispatch decisions | feature | — |
| 5 | WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O — Rotate the whole admissible candidate set with a run-length bound | feature | 1, 2, 3, 4 |
| 6 | WL-0MWKY1CIJ00462ZD — Resolve the gate-asymmetry finding (mechanism b) | task | 1, 5 |
| 7 | WL-0MWKY1GK4001IFUD — Docs: the enforced fair-scheduling rule and its metric | docs | 5, 6 |
| 8 | WL-0MWKY1KL8009PS7K — Re-measure dispatch concentration after the fix | task | 5, 6, 7 |

AC → child map: AC1 → 3, 5, 7 · AC2 → 1, 5, 6 · AC3 → 4 · AC4 → 2 ·
AC5 → 8 · AC6 → 1 (with 2, 3, 4) · AC7 → 7 · AC8 → 8 (final gate).

data.description:
# Worklog pane startup panic misdiagnoses the cause and prescribes the wrong fix

## User story

As a developer hitting a Worklog pane startup failure, I want the panic message
to name the real cause and the command that actually fixes it, so I do not waste
time on a fix that cannot work.

## Problem

`formatStartupError` in `packages/herdr/src/start.ts` treats **every**
"does not provide an export named" error as a stale `@worklog/shared`, printing:

```
The plugin loaded a STALE copy of the shared Worklog code:
  The requested module './downtime-worker.constants.js' does not provide an export named 'DEFAULT_COORDINATION_STALE_WINDOW_MS'
This usually means `packages/shared/dist` was built before the current source.
Rebuild and re-link from the repository root:
      npm run build
```

In the incident that prompted this item the missing module was a **local herdr
module** (`./downtime-worker.constants.js`), not `@worklog/shared`. At incident
time `npm run build` at the repo root did **not** compile `packages/herdr`, so
the prescribed fix could never have worked. Two rebuild attempts were made
before the real cause (a bad merge resolution) was found.

The message is well-intentioned but its diagnosis is unconditional, and it is
the only guidance an operator gets.

> **Update 2026-11-22 (re-plan pass):** the *prescription* half of the incident
> has since been fixed by WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV (completed) — the repo-root
> `npm run build` now compiles `packages/herdr` via `build:herdr`, and a root
> `typecheck` script now exists. The *diagnosis* half is unchanged and still
> wrong: a local missing-export still prints "STALE copy of the shared Worklog
> code" and points at `packages/shared`. This item therefore remains valid as a
> diagnostic-accuracy fix. AC1 was relaxed on 2026-11-22 (producer-approved):
> the local branch still prescribes the targeted plugin build, but may mention
> the repo-root build as a fallback now that it compiles the plugin (see Q5 in
> the Appendix).

## Desired change

- Distinguish the specifier: an `@worklog/shared` import → keep the current
  stale-shared guidance; a **relative** import → the plugin's own source and
  build output disagree, so prescribe the herdr package build
  (`npm run build --prefix packages/herdr`, or the `typecheck` script from the
  sibling prevention item).
- Keep the message actionable and short, and never claim a single cause when the
  evidence does not support it.
- Cover both branches with unit tests (sharing/source mismatch vs local module).

## Acceptance criteria

- A local (relative-specifier) missing-export error names `packages/herdr` and
  prescribes `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr` as the targeted fix; it
  does not name `packages/shared` and does not present the repo-root
  `npm run build` as *the* fix. Since WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV the root build also
  compiles the plugin, so the local branch may mention it as a fallback — but
  the targeted plugin build is the primary command.
- An `@worklog/shared` missing-export error keeps naming the shared package and
  keeps the existing repo-root `npm run build` guidance.
- All three kinds are unit-tested: shared, local, and unattributable/other-bare
  (which must claim no single cause); the non-missing-export branch is unit-
  tested as unchanged too.
- No regression in the existing launcher behaviour (the launcher still exits
  non-zero, and the pane stays open on a TTY so the message can be read).

## Impact

A startup failure now points at the real cause and the command that fixes it,
instead of sending the user down a dead end.

## Discovered from

Diagnosing a Worklog pane startup failure caused by code dropped in merge
`485b764c7`.
## Plan (2026-11-17)

Planning verdict: **no decomposition.** The change is one pure formatter
function in `packages/herdr/src/start.ts` plus its tests and docs (~8 h with
overheads), so the plan is the ordered work sequence below rather than child
work items — the same shape as its completed sibling WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q and
its open sibling WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV, neither of which carries children.

### Existing state (verified on the working tree, 2026-11-17; re-verified 2026-11-22)

- `formatStartupError` (`packages/herdr/src/start.ts`) sets `isMissingExport`
  from `/does not provide an export named/i` and emits the **shared-only**
  diagnosis (stale `@worklog/shared`, repo-root `npm run build`). Every other
  failure takes the generic branch (original message + `npm run build` hint +
  `npm install --prefix packages/herdr` fallback).
- The specifier **is** present in the error text and is machine-readable. Node
  22 and tsx 4.21 under `"type": "module"` (as in `packages/herdr`) emit exactly:
  `The requested module './local-partial.mjs' does not provide an export named 'MISSING'`
  — single-quoted specifier, verified against the real resolver by probe.
- Existing coverage: `tests/unit/start-launcher.test.ts` (canonical suite)
  already unit-tests the formatter's shared branch and drives the real launcher
  end-to-end against `packages/herdr/src/__fixtures__/stale-entry.ts` (plus
  `stale-shared.mjs`), asserting exit code 1 and the diagnostic. That harness is
  reusable verbatim for a relative-specifier case: a sibling
  `local-partial.mjs` + `stale-local-entry.ts` pair reproduces
  `The requested module './local-partial.mjs' does not provide an export named ...`
  under tsx (verified).
- `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr` resolves to the herdr package
  (`npm prefix --prefix packages/herdr` → `<repo>/packages/herdr`) and runs its
  `build` script (`build:shared` → `tsc` → copy shortcuts + chmod), so the
  prescribed command exists and does compile the plugin. **Re-verified
  2026-11-22:** since WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV the repo-root `npm run build` *also*
  compiles `packages/herdr` (`build:herdr` → the plugin's `build:only`), and a
  root `typecheck` script exists (`typecheck:root`/`:shared`/`:herdr`, all
  `--noEmit`). The incident-time statement that the root build "never compiles
  `packages/herdr`" is therefore no longer true.

### Decisions (recorded; conservative, no producer input required)

- **D1 — prescribe only commands that remedy the fault.** The local-branch
  message prescribes `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr`. It does **not**
  prescribe the root `typecheck` script: though that script now exists (since
  WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV), `typecheck:*` runs `tsc --noEmit`, so it reports a type
  error but does **not** rewrite stale `dist/` output — it cannot fix a
  missing-export crash. The build command is the correct remedy. AC1 is refined
  accordingly.
- **D2 — classify by the specifier, not by the module that failed.** Three
  kinds: `shared` (`@worklog/shared…`), `local` (`.`, `..` or an absolute path)
  and `unknown` (no specifier could be extracted, or another bare package). A
  single cause is claimed only for `shared` and `local`.
- **D3 — the launcher contract is unchanged.** `launch()` keeps exit code 1,
  stderr and the TTY-gated keep-open; only the text of the diagnostic changes
  (AC4).
- **D4 — keep the message short.** ≤ ~10 lines per branch, always carrying the
  original error detail verbatim.
- **D5 — no decomposition** (see the verdict above). Test-first ordering is the
  four phases below.
- **D6 — the root build may be a fallback, not the headline (2026-11-22,
  producer-approved).** WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV made the repo-root `npm run build`
  compile `packages/herdr`, so it now *would* fix a local drift. AC1's absolute
  prohibition was therefore evidence-free and was relaxed: the plugin build
  stays the primary, targeted prescription; the root build may be mentioned as a
  fallback. Keeping the prohibition would repeat this item's own defect —
  asserting a limitation the evidence no longer supports.

### Message contract (implementation target)

| Kind | Evidence in the error text | Diagnosis | Prescribed command |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shared` | specifier begins `@worklog/shared` | stale shared build (text unchanged) | `npm run build` (repo root) |
| `local` | specifier begins `./`, `../` or `/` | the plugin's own module and its build output disagree — names `packages/herdr` | `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr` (primary; repo-root `npm run build` may be noted as a fallback) |
| `unknown` | no quoted specifier, or a different bare package | no single cause is claimed; both rebuilds offered | both commands |

The `local` text must point at the plugin package build as the targeted remedy
and state that the failure is in the plugin's own module, not `packages/shared`.
It must **not** present the repo-root `npm run build` as *the* fix — but since
WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV the root build also compiles the plugin, it may be named as
a secondary fallback (AC1, D6). The wording must never claim the root build
cannot fix it. The `unknown` text must claim neither a stale shared build nor a
stale local build.

### Ordered work sequence (test-first)

Every test phase is authored and observed RED before the implementation phase
that makes it green.

1. **Phase 1 — RED unit tests** in `tests/unit/start-launcher.test.ts` (the
   `formatStartupError` describe block):
   - relative specifier → names `packages/herdr`, contains
     `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr`, and contains neither
     `STALE copy of the shared Worklog code` nor `packages/shared/dist`;
   - if the local branch also mentions the repo-root `npm run build`, it is
     labelled a fallback (the plugin build remains the primary command) — a
     standalone assertion on the local branch's wording;
   - `@worklog/shared` specifier → shared guidance unchanged (anti-regression);
   - unattributable / other-bare specifier → no single-cause wording, both
     commands present;
   - non-missing-export error → generic branch unchanged (existing assertion);
   - non-`Error` throw → unchanged (existing assertion).

   Verify: the new assertions are RED and every currently-green assertion stays
   green.
2. **Phase 2 — RED end-to-end test + fixtures.** Add
   `packages/herdr/src/__fixtures__/local-partial.mjs` (exports only a different
   name) and `stale-local-entry.ts` (imports a missing name from
   `./local-partial.mjs`), then extend the `pane launcher (src/start.ts,
   end-to-end)` block: exit code 1, the relative-specifier diagnostic, the herdr
   build command, and prompt exit with stdin closed (the AC4 keep-open
   behaviour is TTY-gated, so the closed-stdin case must not hang).

   Verify: the new e2e case is RED before the implementation phase.
3. **Phase 3 — implementation** in `packages/herdr/src/start.ts`:
   - extract the quoted specifier (`/The requested module ['"]([^'"]+)['"]/i`,
     tolerant of both quote styles; an absent match yields `unknown`) and
     classify it;
   - branch the message per the table; leave `launch()`, `waitForDismiss()` and
     the entry-point detection untouched.

   Verify: Phases 1 and 2 are green; the existing shared-branch and e2e tests
   stay green.
4. **Phase 4 — docs.** `packages/herdr/README.md` § *Development* (the
   `src/start.ts` note) and § *The Worklog tab closes immediately on open*
   (Troubleshooting): describe both causes and both commands. Note that the
   Troubleshooting section currently presents only the stale-shared cause.
   Update the `start.ts` header comment, which currently presents the
   stale-shared case as the only cause.

   Verify: no remaining text claims the shared build is the only cause
   (`grep -rin "stale copy of the shared" packages/herdr/`), and the docs do not
   claim the repo-root build fails to compile the plugin (WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV
   made that false).

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/start.ts` — the formatter and its header comment.
- `tests/unit/start-launcher.test.ts` — formatter unit tests + launcher e2e.
- `packages/herdr/src/__fixtures__/local-partial.mjs` — new fixture module.
- `packages/herdr/src/__fixtures__/stale-local-entry.ts` — new fixture entry.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Development + Troubleshooting wording.

### Constraints

- Do not change `launch()`, `waitForDismiss()`, the entry-point detection, the
  TTY gating or the exit code (AC4).
- Do not add a dependency or a new command script: the fix is message text plus
  a specifier classifier.
- Do not weaken the existing shared-branch text — the shared case is still
  correct, and its tests are the anti-regression guard.
- Do not prescribe the root `typecheck` script as a remedy: it is `--noEmit` and
  cannot repair stale `dist/` (D1). It may be mentioned only as a pre-commit
  prevention step, never as the fix for this crash.

### Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — error-text drift across Node versions.** Node 22 quotes the specifier
  with `'`; a future version could change the phrasing. *Mitigation:* the
  extractor tolerates both quote styles and treats an unmatched specifier as
  `unknown`, which claims no single cause — still correct, just less specific.
- **R2 — tsx resolves TS specifiers (`.js` → `.ts`).** The incident specifier was
  a relative `.js` naming a `.ts` source; both are relative, so classification is
  unaffected. *Mitigation:* fixtures use `.mjs` (as the existing shared fixture
  does), which the ESM linker checks without rewriting — verified with tsx 4.21.
- **A1 — `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr` is the right prescription.**
  Verified: the herdr `build` script exists and `--prefix` resolves from the repo
  root; it compiles `packages/shared` first, so it repairs both a stale plugin
  build and a stale shared build.
- **A2 — the new assertions are gate-enforced.** `tests/unit/start-launcher.test.ts`
  is in the canonical suite (`tests`), so no change to `groups.herdr` is needed.

### Out of scope

  root `typecheck` script — WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV, **now completed** (both landed;
  this item does not re-do them).
- Changing the pane-launch manifest or herdr's own error reporting.
- Any change to the `@worklog/shared` link/refresh mechanics — WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q
  owns that.

### Dependencies

- None blocking. `npm run build --prefix packages/herdr` exists today, so this
  item does not wait on anything.
- WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV **is now completed** (root build compiles the plugin; root
  `typecheck` exists). This item's docs phase must therefore *not* repeat the
  stale claim that the root build does not compile the plugin.

### Duplicate-work check

No overlapping open or completed item. `wl search` on startup / herdr /
typecheck / "export named" returned: WL-0MWKQ4DO2004C03A (restore the code a bad
merge dropped, completed — the incident, not the diagnostic), WL-0MVAY631M004RZ3Q
(added the launcher and its shared-only diagnostic, completed — its AC3 covers
only a *shared* export, so its ACs are not satisfied here),
WL-0MSNULGSM00018I4 (missing `marked` package, completed — a different error
class) and WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV (the typecheck gate, **completed** — it fixed the
prescription/reachability half, not the diagnostic text). Re-checked
2026-11-22: no new item addresses the diagnostic branch.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-17 — plan pass (agent, non-interactive downtime dispatch): added this
  plan block, the message contract, the four-phase test-first work sequence, Key
  Files, constraints, risks, out-of-scope, dependencies and the duplicate-work
  check. Refined AC1 (the `typecheck` alternative is not prescribed because the
  script does not exist — D1), AC2 (names the existing root command explicitly)
  and AC3/AC4 ("all three kinds"; exit-code plus TTY keep-open). No children
  created (D5).

  `intake_complete`, so the plan was re-validated against the current tree.
  Corrections, all fact-driven (no intent change): (a) WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV
  completed, so the root `npm run build` *now* compiles `packages/herdr` and a
  root `typecheck` script exists — the Problem note, Existing state, D1,

  (c) the work sequence was reordered so the e2e test is authored RED *before*
  the implementation (the old Phase 3 verify clause contradicted its own
  ordering); (d) the duplicate-work check and Appendix Q1 were re-verified. No
  children created (D5 unchanged).

  blanket "does not prescribe the repo-root `npm run build`" clause rested on a

# Placement gate false-positive blocks epic driving on a busy machine

## Problem statement

`implement.py parent <epic>` refuses to proceed for an epic child whose
worktree exists but holds no changes whenever **any** other registered
worktree of the repository is dirty:

```
ERROR: Child WL-... produced changes in the sibling worktree
.../worktrees/wl-WL-0MVOA0XVC... instead of its worktree ...
Offending paths: ...
```

`_child_main_checkout_violation` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`)
treats "child worktree clean + sibling worktree dirty" as evidence that the
child wrote outside its tree. Condition 3 of its documented precision rule
says pre-existing/unrelated dirt must not block a legitimate child, but the
code only earns that exemption when the child's own worktree already holds
changes — which a **freshly started child never does**. The result: on a
machine running several concurrent dispatches (the normal steady state),
`parent` and `drive` fail closed before the first child session is ever
spawned.

## Evidence (captured 2026-11-18, parent epic WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9)

1. `implement.py parent WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9` started child
   WL-0MWKY141H002LULI and created its (empty) worktree.
2. `implement.py drive WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9` then failed in `phase_parent`
   with one message per dirty sibling worktree:
   - `wl-WL-0MVOA0XVC0002PBG-...` (item soft-deleted, 3 dirty paths)
   - `wl-WL-0MVOBP8MC0093Y7T-...` (blocked item, 22 dirty paths)
   - `wl-WL-0MWKQ51G0006F3KV-...` (live concurrent dispatch, 15 dirty paths)
   - `wl-WL-0MWMGEL5R003IH71-...` (6 dirty paths)
   - `/tmp/wl-base-check`, `/tmp/wl-clean-check`, ... (1 dirty path each)
   `sessions_spawned: 0` — no child session ran, so no child work existed.
3. Removing the empty worktree (`implement.py abort`) and re-running `drive`
   let the chain start normally: `phase_start` recreated the tree and the
   session was spawned, precisely because no clean worktree existed at the
   moment the placement check ran.

## Desired change

A freshly started child (worktree created, no session spawned against it yet)
must never be reported as a placement violation because of dirt in a
*different* work item's worktree. Candidate treatments, in order of
preference:

- Exempt a child whose worktree was created by this run's `phase_start` and
  has never had a session spawned against it (the same shape as the existing
  `read_spawn_failure` exemption).
- Restrict the sibling scan to worktrees whose dirt this child's session could
  have produced (age ordering vs the child worktree creation time).
- At minimum, fail-open (WARNING) when the offending sibling belongs to an
  independently live, non-terminal item (a concurrent dispatch), keeping the
  hard failure only for siblings whose item is terminal (deleted/completed),
  where the dirt genuinely is orphaned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A unit test drives `phase_parent`/`_child_main_checkout_violation` with a
  clean child worktree and at least one dirty sibling worktree owned by a
  distinct non-terminal item and asserts the child is reported startable, not
  failed.
- A second test pins the genuine case that must stay fail-closed: dirt in a
  sibling worktree attributable to this child's own session still fails
  placement.
- `implement.py drive <epic>` completes its first `parent` step and spawns the
  first child session on a repository where other items' worktrees are dirty.
- No existing placement/attribution test regresses.

## Impact

An epic can be driven on a machine that is also running other dispatches,
instead of the driver dead-ending before the first child session.

Discovered from WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 (deps: discovered-from:WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9).


## Related work

- WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 — parent epic from which this bug was discovered (discovered-from).
- WL-0MVPADZ1Z000FOSG — completed guard work on `implement.py finish` wiping the main checkout; same placement/attribution area, no AC overlap.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_child_main_checkout_violation` (~L19973) holds the precision rule (condition 1–3) and the sibling-worktree scan; call sites in `phase_parent`/`phase_drive` (~L15684, ~L15745).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py` — existing stray-write and spawn-failure coverage (`TestDrivenChildStraysIntoSiblingWorktree`, `TestSpawnFailureEvidence`, `TestSpawnFailedChildIsStartableAgain`).
- `skill/implement/tests/test_worktree_has_changes.py` — `_git_path_has_changes`/dirty-path helpers used by the guard.

- **WL-0MQF3H65W003ZGAS** – wl next should show parent instead of descending into child items (completed)
- **WL-0MQF95NCC0024H61** – wl next Stage 3 blocker surfacing still returns child items (completed)

# Validate post-fix dispatch fairness after three days

Earliest run: **2026-11-22T15:30:00Z** (three days after the operator restarted
the downtime dispatcher panes on 2026-11-19T~15:15Z). Until that instant there
is no post-fix window long enough to judge, so this item is scheduled with
`startOn` rather than being dispatched immediately.

Follow-up from **WL-0MWKY1KL8009PS7K** (the post-fix re-measurement, which was
reported *inconclusive* because the live dispatcher was still running pre-fix
code) and from parent **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** AC5.

## Why

The fairness fix (whole-set round-robin rotation + `RUN_LENGTH_CEILING = 2`,
commits `ef46c0bd8` / `7a0d1460c`) is now live: the operator restarted every
Herdr `Work Items` plugin pane, so the dispatcher loads current
`packages/herdr/src`. The only remaining question is whether the live
behaviour actually meets the thresholds over a real window — which needs
elapsed time, not code.

## Users

The operator of the multi-project Herdr workspace (single user, 10 registered
project roots), who relies on the downtime dispatcher to spread agent sessions
evenly instead of letting one project monopolise the slots.

- As the workspace operator, I want a measured pass/fail on the fairness rule
  over a real post-restart window, so that "the fix works" is evidence rather
  than assumption.
- As the workspace operator, I want the measurement reproducible from the logs
  alone, so that a future reader can re-derive it after the logs have rotated.

## Scope

Read-only validation. No code change is expected; if the numbers fail, record
the evidence and file a follow-up work item rather than editing the dispatcher
from this item.

- Confirm from `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` that decision entries now
  carry the fairness metric (`selectedRoot`, and `dispatchingRoot` +
  `consecutiveRunLength` on consumed dispatches) — proof the current code is
  live.
- Measure the window from each project's `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`
  (rows with a `paneId`) using the counting rules recorded in
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- Cross-check the dispatch-log distribution against the decision-log fairness
  metric (the accounting identity).
- Report the result on **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9**.

## Existing state

Captured at intake (2026-11-19T23:35Z) — indicative only; it is **not** the
measurement this item asks for, and the measured window must still be taken
after 2026-11-22T15:30Z.

- **The regime check already passes by observation.** Fairness-bearing decision
  entries (`selectedRoot`) first appear at `2026-11-19T18:01:53.039Z`
  (`projects/tce-the-rising/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`) and, in the
  downtime leader's own log, from `2026-11-19T20:47:02.017Z`
  (`projects/SorraAgents/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`) — both after the
  ~15:15Z restart, so the running code includes the fairness accounting. AC1
  should be re-confirmed against the measured window, not assumed from this.
- The leader's log is where decisions land: 17 fairness-bearing decision rows
  between `2026-11-19T20:47:02Z` and `2026-11-19T23:34:39Z` — 14
  `reason: "dispatched"`, 3 `reason: "reservation-refused"`. Distinct
  `selectedRoot`s: SorraAgents 5, ContextHub 5, AI_Hell 3, tce-the-rising 2,
  games_curator 2 (5 active projects ≥ the three-project floor).
- Every recorded `consecutiveRunLength` in that leader-log window is `1`; the
  only `2` observed today is `2026-11-19T18:17:34.785Z` in
  `projects/tce-the-rising/.worklog/downtime-coordination.log`. 14 dispatches is
  far too small a sample to declare anything.
- **Open point for the measurement:** 2 of the 17 rows record `selectedRoot`
  ≠ `dispatchingRoot` (`18:01:53Z` and `23:18:07Z`). The counting rules charge
  `dispatchingRoot`, so this is either a benign deferral/ordering effect or a
  real accounting-identity mismatch — the AC4 cross-check is where it gets
  settled, and the finding must be stated either way.
- The round-robin cursor file (`~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json`)
  currently lists 10 roots; the recent window served 5 of them.

## Data sources (read-only)

- `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` — per project; the leader's copy carries
  the decision rows (periodically rotated, ~500 lines).
- `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` — per project; dispatch rows carrying a
  `paneId` (rotated, ~500 lines per project — evidence disappears within
  hours, so capture aggregates as soon as they are read).
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json` — cursor state at the
  window boundary.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — the counting rules ("*Counting rules.*"
  section: window, rows, project key, regime check, even share, consecutive
  run, kind mix, accounting identity).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A decision entry carrying `selectedRoot` is observed after the restart
  timestamp, confirming the current code is live.
- A window with at least three active projects is measured, stating the window
  (UTC start/end), the project count and the counting rules used.
- No project exceeds twice its even share of dispatches in that window, and no
  project holds a consecutive run longer than 2.
- The distribution derived from the decision-log fairness metric agrees with
  the dispatch-log aggregates for the same window.
- The table (per-project counts, longest consecutive runs, kind mix) and an
  explicit pass/fail against both thresholds are reported on
  WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9; a fail records the evidence, the suspected cause and a
  follow-up work item.
- If the window has fewer than three active projects, the measurement is
  recorded as inconclusive (with the extended window or the reason it could
  not be extended) rather than declared a pass.
- The captured aggregates and the exact read-only commands/queries used are
  recorded on this work item (not only in the report comment), so the result
  can be re-derived after the logs rotate.
- Any documentation claim that the measurement contradicts (e.g. in
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`) is corrected; if that — or a follow-up fix
  arising from a fail — produces a code or doc change, the full project test
  suite must pass with that change.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Read-only: no dispatcher behaviour change, no gate change, no scheduler
  change.
- Measure only after the restart marker is visible — a window spanning the
  restart would mix two code versions.
- Log rotation (500 lines per project) discards evidence within hours: capture
  the aggregates as soon as they are read and record them on the item.
- Report on a completed parent (**WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9**, `completed`/`in_review`)
  via a comment; do not reopen it.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Small sample.** Rotation keeps ~500 lines per project and the recent rate is
  ~14 dispatches in 3 hours, so a three-day window may still be a thin sample;
  state the dispatch total and do not declare a pass on a handful of rows.
- **Too few active projects.** Overnight/weekend windows can drop below three
  active projects; AC6 already requires recording *inconclusive* rather than a
  pass.
- **Mixed regime.** Any window reaching back past `2026-11-19T18:01Z` mixes the
  pre-fix worker's rows; the window must start after the restart marker.
- **Assumption:** the leader's `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` (currently
  SorraAgents) is the canonical decision log; per-project logs receive only the
  rows that project's pane produced.
- **Assumption:** `dispatchingRoot` is the charged root (the counting rules say
  so), so the two observed `selectedRoot` ≠ `dispatchingRoot` rows are explained
  by deferral/ordering rather than by a defect — AC4 must prove it.
- **Scope-creep risk.** A failing measurement invites an immediate dispatcher
  fix; that is deliberately out of scope here (read-only), so any fix becomes a
  new linked work item with its own ACs and release gate.

## Impact

The operator gets a measured, reproducible verdict on whether the dispatcher's
fixed fair-sharing actually holds live, so even distribution across their
projects is evidenced rather than assumed.

**Key Files:**

- `.worklog/downtime-coordination.log` (per project; read-only) — decision rows; regime check (`selectedRoot`) and accounting identity (`dispatchingRoot`, `consecutiveRunLength`)
- `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (per project; read-only) — dispatch rows with a `paneId`; per-project counts, runs, kind mix
- `~/.herdr/downtime/downtime-round-robin-by-root.json` — cursor state at the window boundary
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — counting rules and thresholds to quote with the result
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-coordination.ts` — where the fairness fields are written (reference only; no change expected)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-entries.ts` — dispatch-row shape (`paneId`, `cwd`, `kind`)

## Related work

- **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** — *Dispatcher seems to unevenly distribute work*
  (completed/in_review) — the epic; AC5 is this validation, and the report goes
  here.
- **WL-0MWKY1KL8009PS7K** — *Re-measure dispatch concentration after the fix*
  (completed/in_review) — the first attempt; reported *inconclusive* because
  the live worker still ran pre-fix code. Its counting methodology and outcome
  section are the template for this item.
- **WL-0MWKY141H002LULI** — *Record per-project fairness metric on dispatch
  decisions* (completed) — added the `selectedRoot`/`dispatchingRoot`/
  `consecutiveRunLength` fields this measurement reads.
- **WL-0MWKY1GK4001IFUD** — *Docs: the enforced fair-scheduling rule and its
  metric* (completed) — the counting rules and metric documentation.
- **WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O** — *Rotate the whole admissible candidate set with a
  run-length bound* (completed) — the fix under test (`RUN_LENGTH_CEILING = 2`).
- **WL-0MWO38U4W002853V** — *Publish fairness report and update documentation*
  (blocked/intake_complete) — downstream consumer of a passing result; blocked,
  so it cannot absorb this measurement.
- Repo docs: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — "Re-measuring concentration
  after a fix" / *Counting rules*.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No interview questions were asked.** The item had been re-scoped by a prior
  `implement` session and already carried a problem statement, scope, six
  testable acceptance criteria, data sources and constraints, so the interview
  was skipped per the intake contract (seed context sufficient to draft).
- **Q: Is this a duplicate of the completed re-measurement (WL-0MWKY1KL8009PS7K)?**
  — Answer (agent research, source: `wl show WL-0MWKY1KL8009PS7K --json`): No.
  That item closed *inconclusive* because the live dispatcher still ran pre-fix
  code; its ACs were therefore not satisfied by observation. This item measures
  a fresh window after the operator's restart, which is the gap it leaves.
  Partial overlap only — no rewrite needed; the description already isolates the
  post-restart window.
- **Q: Is `chore` the right issue type?** — Answer (agent decision): yes — no
  code behaviour changes; this is operational validation plus reporting, with a
  conditional doc correction only on a contradictory finding.
- **Q: Why was the automated `/skill:find-related` report not generated?** —
  Answer (agent research): the script re-claims the item with
  `--status in-progress`, which the `startOn` claim guard
  (`src/claim-start-on.ts`, WL-0MWMGEUT10056MUI) refuses with
  `start_on_not_reached` until 2026-11-22T15:30Z, and it exposes no
  `--force-start-on` passthrough. The `## Related work` list above was therefore
  gathered manually from `wl search` / `wl list --parent` and is idempotent to
  re-run later.

# Fairness across remote dispatching hosts

Investigation item: **examine why one machine obtains a disproportionate share
of the shared dispatch slots when several hosts dispatch at once, and present
potential solutions.** The deliverable is an evidence-backed RCA plus an options
paper with one recommendation — implementation is deferred to follow-up items
(including a cross-repo proxy item where required).

## Problem statement

When more than one host runs downtime dispatchers against the same shared
llama-proxy, one machine consistently holds an unfair share of the scarce local
GPU slots: its panes occupy slot time while other hosts' dispatchable work waits
or is never dispatched. The suspicion is that the winning host is simply the one
running more dispatcher instances / agent panes, because slot arbitration is
keyed to the **session**, not to the **host** — so a host's share grows with the
number of sessions it happens to have live.

## Users

- **As the producer**, I want idle capacity shared across hosts on a rule I can
  state and verify, so that a machine running many dispatchers does not
  monopolise the GPU slot budget at the expense of a machine running one.
- **As a project owner whose work sits on a starved host**, I want to see from
  the logs *why* my host got no slot (host-share, lease retention, budget, or a
  safety gate) rather than guessing.
- **As the dispatcher maintainer**, I want the fairness invariant enforced (or
  at least measured and documented) by the code path that actually grants a
  slot, with a way to detect regression from the recorded evidence.
- **As the proxy maintainer**, I want any host-aware arbitration to reuse the
  existing lease/queue machinery and the existing client-identity logging,
  without adding a second scheduler.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A per-host measurement is recorded on this work item: for one documented
  window with at least two participating hosts, a table of, per host,
  dispatched-pane count, local slot-seconds held, active vs. retained (idle)
  lease time and share of total; the data sources (proxy structured logs with
  `client_ip`, per-host downtime dispatch logs, lease events) and the exact
  queries used are documented so an auditor can reproduce the table.
- A root-cause analysis names every mechanism that can push a host's share above
  a fair share, with code references and evidence, or rules it out with
  evidence. At minimum evaluate: (a) session-keyed lease acquisition with
  same-session re-acquisition and non-preemptive idle-lease retention; (b) a
  host's share scaling with its number of dispatcher instances / live panes;
  (c) the free-slot gate reading one global slot snapshot, so the earliest or
  fastest poller wins; (d) the absence of any host-keyed slot accounting today.
- A definition of "fair" is documented and justified, stating explicitly how it
  treats hosts with **different numbers of dispatcher instances** (the
  invariant to hold: a host's share must not scale with its instance count) and
  hosts with different capacity, plus what happens when a host has no
  dispatchable work.
- At least two candidate solutions are presented with trade-offs, each naming
  the component it changes (herdr dispatcher vs. llama-proxy), its failure
  modes, its fail-open behaviour, and whether it needs a cross-repo proxy change
  (a new `LP-` work item) or can be done dispatcher-side; the options must
  include at least one that works without a proxy change.
- One recommendation is made — the smallest change that makes host share
  independent of instance count — with its residual risks and the follow-up
  work items required to implement it recorded and linked (this item does not
  implement it).
- Validation: every quantitative claim in the report is reproducible from a
  documented command or query on a named host; any helper script added for the
  measurement has a unit test covering its reduction logic.
- Fairness cannot regress the existing dispatch gates: critical-first,
  review-queue depth, code-freeze, host-CPU gate, host dispatch budget and the
  audit tier must be shown to behave exactly as today (by inspection of the
  proposed change surface, since this item ships no behaviour change).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The operator can see, host by host, how shared dispatch capacity is actually
distributed and why one machine dominates — and gets a single change that makes
each host's share depend on the work it has, not on how many dispatchers happen
to be running there.

## Constraints

- **Investigation, not a scheduler rewrite.** Deliver measured evidence, a
  fairness definition, options and one recommendation. Record implementation as
  follow-up items rather than doing it here.
- **Cross-repo boundary.** Proxy arbitration lives in `llm-manager` (`LP-`
  prefix, e.g. `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`); herdr-side work must not assume a
  new proxy contract exists. Any host-aware arbitration that must run in the
  proxy needs its own `LP-` work item and a version-tolerant client.
- **Fail-open.** Any new accounting or arbitration must never refuse a dispatch
  because a read, lock or log parse failed; a failure degrades to today's
  behaviour.
- **Hot-path budget.** No additional `wl` spawn per tick; measurement runs
  off-log, not in the dispatch loop.
- **Gates preserved.** Critical-first, review-queue, code-freeze, host-CPU gate,
  host dispatch budget and audit admission keep their current precedence;
  fairness never buys itself by relaxing a safety gate.
- **No unilateral cap changes.** Changing per-host `budget.json` defaults
  (`maxImplement: 2`, `maxAudit: 1`) or the proxy's `session_slot_pool_size` is
  a producer decision; the options paper must quantify such a change rather than
  apply it.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: wrong resource.** If "slots" turns out not to be the proxy's local
  slots, the measurement AC still surfaces the real contention point (AC1
  requires both slot-seconds and dispatched-pane counts per host); the options
  paper must then address whatever the data shows.
- **Risk: measurement needs a quiet or attributable window.** Proxy logs carry
  `client_ip`, but a `local-preferred` request routed to a remote provider never
  holds a local slot, so slot-seconds and dispatch counts must be reported
  separately to avoid a misleading ratio.
- **Risk: proxy change is a separate release train.** A host-aware lease needs
  an `LP-` item and a version-tolerant herdr client; the dispatcher-side option
  is the fallback if the proxy change stalls.
- **Risk: fairness versus throughput.** Per-host caps can idle the GPU when one
  host has all the work; the options paper must quantify the idle cost of each
  option rather than trading throughput silently.
- **Scope-creep guard:** fixing per-host fairness in code, changing
  `budget.json` defaults, changing `session_slot_pool_size`, or building a
  dashboard is **out of scope** — record each as a linked follow-up item.
- **Assumption A1–A4** are recorded in the appendix and need producer
  confirmation at review; none blocks starting the investigation.

## Existing state

- **Dispatch-side fairness is per machine, by construction.** The coordination
  dir, leader election and dispatch-budget ledger are single-machine
  (`~/.herdr/downtime/`, `machine-coordination.ts`); the docs state the local
  coordination/ledger paths are single-machine and that only the audit budget is
  cross-machine, via the proxy. Per-host caps today are `maxImplement: 2` /
  legacy `maxAudit: 1` in `budget.json`.
- **The genuinely shared resource across hosts is the proxy's local slots.** The
  dispatcher's free-slot gate reads one **global** slot snapshot from
  `GET {proxyUrl}/llama/local/status`; whoever polls and dispatches first takes
  the slot.
- **Slot arbitration is session-keyed, not host-keyed.**
  `_try_acquire_local_dispatch(srv, max_local, session_key, …)` admits up to
  `session_slot_pool_size` concurrent sessions; same-session re-acquisition is
  always permitted, and the no-preemption policy lets an inactive (post-request
  cooldown) lease keep reserving its slot for the owning session. Nothing in the
  lease record names the host.
- **Host attribution exists only in logs.** The proxy resolves and logs
  `client_ip` / `client_ip_source` / `client_port` on status and lease events
  (LP-0MSKV3IEQ004ZV88), so per-host slot-seconds are measurable after the fact,
  but no arbitration or accounting path consumes host identity.
- **Per-project rotation already exists and is single-machine.** The
  least-recently-served root ordering with a twice-in-succession run-length
  bound (`downtime-worker.fairness.ts`, WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9 /
  WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O) fixes *project* concentration on one host; it has no
  notion of a host and cannot arbitrate across machines.
- **Prior attribution incident.** A 2026-08 investigation (WL-0MSKUF67I003U02T)
  found ~8 un-attributable `status_request` pollers, 3–4 concurrent connections
  from a single remote host; client-IP logging was added as the fix. That is the
  precedent for measuring rather than guessing.

## Desired change

A published report (e.g. `docs/dev/cross-host-slot-fairness.md`, linked from
`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`) containing: the per-host share measurement
and its methodology, the fairness definition and invariant, the root-cause
findings with code references, the candidate solutions with trade-offs and a
recommendation, and links to the follow-up implementation items. No behaviour
change in this item.

**Key Files:**

- `docs/dev/cross-host-slot-fairness.md` — new report: measurement, fairness definition, root causes, options, recommendation
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — cross-host fairness section/link; correct any "single-machine only" wording that measurement contradicts
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-cpu-gate.ts` — global free-slot gate (candidate dispatcher-side lever); inspect for the host-count interaction, no change expected
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — per-host ledger/caps (`maxImplement`, `maxAudit`) referenced by the options paper, no change expected
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — machine-scope contract and its doc comment (any wording change)
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — existing per-host observability surface, candidate place to surface host share
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fairness.ts` — per-project rotation (contrast: why it cannot arbitrate across hosts)
- `llm-manager/proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` session-keyed leases (proxy-side option; cross-repo `LP-` item)
- `llm-manager/proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `_resolve_client_ip` / `_resolve_client_id`, the host-attribution seam used for measurement
- `llm-manager/proxy/docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` — existing fairness discussion (per-session FIFO), the design context for any proxy-side option

## Related work

- **WL-0MWKE9VF800101V9** (completed) — dispatcher unevenly distributes work
  across *projects* on one machine; measured the same class of concentration and
  produced the round-robin/run-length fixes. This item is the cross-*host*
  analogue and must reuse its measurement style.
- **WL-0MWKY1839000JM5O** (completed) — whole-set rotation with a run-length
  bound; establishes the "no new scheduler" precedent.
- **WL-0MWFIZ8H5005FVNN** (completed) — post-dispatch cursor charge; how the
  previous fairness defect was diagnosed from decision logs.
- **WL-0MTYZXSLN008HZOW** (completed) — over-dispatch on a single-slot LLM:
  per-tick free-slot polling versus the proxy owner lease. Closest existing
  analysis of slot-vs-dispatch accounting.
- **WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA** (completed) — host-wide audit slot saturation from
  concurrent audits; the precedent that a shared proxy resource needs
  cross-instance coordination.
- **WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS** (completed) — proxy-owned audit budget: the one
  existing cross-machine serialisation pattern to imitate or extend.
- **WL-0MSKUF67I003U02T** (completed) — poller attribution on proxy:8000;
  produced the `client_ip` logging this measurement depends on.
- **WL-0MSKUG2WI004CBW3** (completed) — dispatch logs/leases on the remote
  host filesystem; where per-host dispatch evidence lives.
- **WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P** (completed) — truthful per-slot capacity consumption
  (`lease_state` / `capacity_hint`), the semantics of "a slot" in this codebase.
- **WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK** (completed) — RCA: herdr round-robin dispatch across
  multiple projects not working; the earlier defect family this item must not
  re-litigate for the per-host case.
- **WL-0MWKY1GK4001IFUD** (completed) — docs for the enforced fair-scheduling
  rule and its metric; the documented-metric precedent to follow.
- **llm-manager `LP-0MSKV3IEQ004ZV88`** (proxy) — client-identity logging
  (completed proxy side); the attribution prerequisite.
- **docs**: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (host budget, proxy-derived audit
  admission, free-slot gate), `packages/herdr/README.md` (downtime settings),
  `llm-manager/proxy/docs/dev/slot-management-design.md` and
  `llm-manager/proxy/docs/dev/contention-queue-*.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

This intake was dispatched automatically by the herdr downtime worker
(`herdr-downtime`, session id recorded on the work item), so no interactive
producer round was available. Questions are recorded below with the documented
assumption used and marked for producer confirmation at review; none of them
blocks the investigation this item scopes.

- Q: What exactly is a "slot" here — the shared llama-proxy local-GPU slots, or
  the per-host dispatch opportunity on the shared backlog?
  — Assumption A1 (agent, from repo evidence): the shared **proxy local slots**
  (llama-server slots / local dispatch leases). Rationale: "slot" is used that
  way throughout `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` ("free-slot gate", "slot
  budget", `lease_state`), the dispatch budget is already per-host, and the only
  resource that is genuinely shared across hosts is the proxy GPU. AC1 requires
  measuring **both** slot-seconds and dispatched-pane counts per host, so the
  analysis identifies the real contention point instead of assuming it.
  Source: repo search (`packages/herdr/src`, `llm-manager/proxy`).
  Status: **OPEN QUESTION — confirm at review.**
- Q: Is the deliverable a report with proposed solutions, or a code change?
  — Answer (agent, from the item description): the description says "examine why
  this is and present potential solutions", so the deliverable is an
  evidence-backed RCA plus an options paper with one recommendation; the
  code change is recorded as follow-up work items. Source: item description.
  Status: accepted; revisit at review if the producer wants the fix in scope.
- Q: Must the fix be dispatcher-side (herdr) only, or may it require a proxy
  change in `llm-manager`?
  — Assumption A2 (agent): both may be proposed, but at least one option must be
  dispatcher-side, and any proxy change must be split into its own `LP-` item
  because this is a `WL-` (ContextHub) work item and the repos are separate.
  Source: repo boundary evidence (`llm-manager` has its own `LP-` worklog).
  Status: **OPEN QUESTION — confirm at review.**
- Q: How should "fair" be weighted when hosts have different numbers of
  dispatcher instances (and possibly different capacity)?
  — Assumption A3 (agent): the invariant to hold is that a host's share must
  **not** scale with its instance count; equal-share-per-host is the baseline,
  with capacity-weighting presented as an explicit alternative. The options paper
  quantifies both. Source: item description ("different machines may have
  different numbers of the dispatcher running").
  Status: **OPEN QUESTION — confirm at review.**
- Q: Which hosts and which proxy are in scope for the measurement?
  — Assumption A4 (agent): the ContextHub hosts that dispatch to the shared
  proxy (default `downtimeProxyUrl` `http://192.168.0.199:8000`) and any remote
  host whose `client_ip` appears in proxy logs during the window. Source:
  `packages/herdr/README.md` (proxy default), WL-0MSKUF67I003U02T (remote host
  evidence). Status: recorded; the window is chosen in the report.

# Hygiene: a registered worktree whose owning work item no longer resolves is unreportable debris

## Problem Statement

Discovered-from WL-0MWQLHDOS006CAIH (stale scratch worktrees blocking the
placement guard). Two debris classes are now filtered by the guard (outside the
repository's worktree root; owning item terminal) and reported by
`scripts/hygiene_check.sh`. A **third** class is not covered: a registered
worktree whose directory name carries a work-item id that `wl show` cannot
resolve — it exists in no worklog.

Observed in the SorraAgents checkout (2026-11-21, after the parent item's fix
landed): of eight dirty registered siblings, exactly one still counted as a
foreign change surface —
`.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MVTUD4HS000O6AB-prose-blocked-by-and-cross-project-block`
— because `wl show SA-0MVTUD4HS000O6AB` returns "Work item not found". The
guard correctly **fails closed** (unresolved ownership is never silently
ignored, by design), and the hygiene check reports nothing for it (reporting
only, never guessing). The net effect is that this one tree can still refuse a
clean epic child until an operator removes it by hand — the same operational
stall the parent item removed for the other two classes.

## Desired Change

Decide, with a documented rule, what to do with a tree whose owning item does
not resolve:

- **Report it.** `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` should surface it as a third debris
  class (e.g. `unresolved_owner`) with the same prune remedy and the same
  non-warning (exit-code-neutral) semantics, so an operator can see it.
- **Keep the guard fail-closed.** The placement guard must keep counting the
  surface unless a deliberate, safe rule (for example: registered under the
  canonical root AND untouched for longer than a documented age) allows it to
  be discounted. Deleting, pruning or resetting trees remains an operator
  decision — never automatic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` reports registered worktrees under the
  repository's worktree root whose owning work item does not resolve, in text
  and `--json`, with the prune remedy; existing checks, exit codes and the
  debris notice's non-warning semantics are unchanged.
- The placement guard's behaviour for such a tree is documented (currently:
  fail closed) and pinned by a test.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` documents the class and the remedy.
- Full test suite green.

## Key Files

- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` (`check_debris_worktrees`)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`_is_live_foreign_surface`,
  `_worktree_owner_is_terminal`)
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`
- `tests/test_implement_stash_hygiene.py`,
  `skill/implement/tests/test_drive_sibling_worktree_stray.py`

## Impact

An operator can see — and remove — the last class of stale tree that can still
refuse a clean epic child in an old checkout, instead of hitting a refusal with
no report explaining it.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-11-21 22:06 UTC** — Plan skill pre-check returned `skip` (Small effort, Low risk). Six automated review stages completed against existing content; AC coverage review proceeded (fully covered). No child work items created — item is sufficiently sized for direct implementation.

No clarifying questions were raised. The item was sufficiently defined for direct implementation.
